headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure to large energy users, preventing residential ratepayers from subsidizing their expansion.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, environmental groups.
opponents: Large energy users (data centers), utility companies.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines.
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission ruled that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure they require, preventing these costs from falling on residential ratepayers. This decision, supported by Governor Abigail Spanberger, is projected to save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This bill requires waterworks operators to categorize and report water sales data, including usage by data centers, to increase transparency for state water planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Sierra Club), local communities, water conservation advocates, State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting.
news_summary: New regulations, taking effect January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize monthly sales data, including water usage by data centers, to provide more transparency for state environmental planning. This bill, carried by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill a data gap and aid the Department of Environmental Quality in water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise impacts and allows localities to demand information on other environmental effects before approving large data centers.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental groups (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters).
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia cracks down on data center water and noise.
news_summary: Virginia has approved new rules for data centers, including tighter regulations on water use and noise, in response to growing resident complaints. The Department of Environmental Quality is tasked with setting the state's first data center noise standard by 2029, with violations leading to significant fines.
